option.counterfactual: Every faithful normalized 2-quasitrace on a finite AW*-factor is exhaustive: positive elements with partial sums bounded by 1 must have quasitrace values tending to zero.
option.approach: Apply exhaustivity to the differences a_(n+1)-a_n to prove that the set is empty. This would avoid all questions about least upper bounds.

judge.reason: It claims an exact value for the set, identical to the answer in e1.

options.counterfactual: A faithful normalized 2-quasitrace on a finite AW*-factor can fail exhaustivity: there can be positive elements with partial sums bounded by 1 whose quasitrace values do not tend to zero.
options.approach: Extract terms whose quasitrace values have a uniform positive lower bound, then rescale each term to obtain constant quasitrace increments. Investigate whether a quasitracial ultrapower preserves the factor hypotheses and ensures that the resulting increasing sequence has no least upper bound.

options.approach: Verify a structural theorem with exactly these hypotheses and use it to exclude the required absence of a least upper bound. Distinguish this theorem explicitly from completeness of the projection lattice.
